headline: MP MATERIALS CROSSES 1,000 MT NdPr THRESHOLD — Q3 Revenue $147.7M; GM Magnet Qualification Done, Sales Start Q4
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) reported Q3 2026 results on November 5, posting $147.7 million in revenue — up from $108.5 million in Q2 — with NdPr production hitting 1,018 metric tonnes, the first quarter above the 1,000 MT milestone and a 41% increase year over year. The company confirmed completion of its General Motors magnet qualification process, with saleable deliveries and revenue beginning in Q4 2026.

headline: IAMGOLD Q3: CÔTÉ GOLD SLIPS TO 64,400 oz — Below Year-Ago Record; Full-Year Guidance Cut to Lower End; Conf Call This Morning
snippet: IAMGOLD Corporation (TSX: IMG) released Q3 2026 results after market close on November 5, with Côté Gold Mine producing 64,400 attributable ounces — below the year-ago record of roughly 106,000 ounces — bringing year-to-date Côté output to 184,000 attributable ounces and placing full-year guidance firmly at the lower end of the 270,000–310,000-ounce range. IAMGOLD holds its Q3 earnings conference call at 8:30 a.m. ET this morning (November 6).

headline: FREEPORT APPROVES $4.5B BAGDAD COPPER EXPANSION — Doubles Arizona Output to 400Mlbs/yr; Becomes U.S.'s 2nd-Largest Copper Mine
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan's (NYSE: FCX) board of directors approved the $4.5 billion Bagdad Copper expansion on November 4, authorizing a brownfield project that would more than double the Arizona mine's output to over 400 million pounds of copper per year — an increase of roughly 225 million pounds — plus more than 12 million additional pounds of molybdenum. When complete, Bagdad ranks as the second-largest copper mine in the United States, behind only Morenci, and the economics are supported at an incentive copper price of approximately $4.00 per pound.

headline: ROYAL GOLD RECORD ROYALTY QUARTER — $464.8M Revenue, $344.4M Operating Cash Flow; 109K GEOs Sold, Dividend Up 6%
snippet: Royal Gold (NASDAQ: RGLD) posted record Q3 2026 operating cash flow of $344.4 million — almost double the $174.0 million generated a year earlier — alongside revenue of $464.8 million and net income of $227.4 million ($2.68/share). The royalty and streaming company sold a record 109,000 gold-equivalent ounces, raised its quarterly dividend 6% to $0.475/share, and repaid $250 million on its revolving credit facility, lifting available liquidity to roughly $1.48 billion.

headline: GOLD $4,121 AS BANK OF ENGLAND HIKES — Dollar Drop Trumps Rate Headwind; Silver Lags at $52.78 as Ratio Widens
snippet: Spot gold climbed to $4,121 per ounce on November 5 — rising 1.5% even as the Bank of England raised rates — confirming gold's decoupling from rate-sensitive pressure when dollar weakness is the dominant force. Silver advanced more modestly to $52.78, widening the gold-silver ratio to 78.1, as gold has now recovered nearly $250 from October's intraday low near $3,875.

headline: NICKEL SURGES TO 5-WEEK HIGH — Indonesia's Top Mine Hits Annual Quota and Halts; Supply Crunch Deepens
snippet: Nickel prices jumped to a five-week high after Indonesia's largest nickel mine exhausted its 2026 annual production quota and was forced to halt ore extraction — the latest consequence of a government quota crackdown that has tightened supply across the sector. Indonesia, which accounts for more than half of global nickel mine output, has cut annual quotas throughout 2026, with Weda Bay Nickel among the operations that have suspended production after depleting their allocated tonnage.

headline: CRITICAL METALS CLOSES EUROPEAN LITHIUM BID — Tanbreez REE Greenland Mining Permit Through 2050 Consolidated; 90.5M Shares Issued
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (NASDAQ: CRML) completed its acquisition of European Lithium on November 5 after court-approved schemes transferred all shares and listed options to the buyer. The 90.5-million-share deal consolidates Critical Metals' ownership of the Wolfsberg lithium project in Austria and the Tanbreez rare earth project in Greenland, which recently received authorization for mining through September 2050.

headline: TALISKER FILES BRALORNE GOLD PEA — Fully Permitted BC High-Grade Project Gets NI 43-101 Economic Assessment
snippet: Talisker Resources (TSX: TSK) announced the filing of a National Instrument 43-101 Preliminary Economic Assessment for its fully permitted Bralorne Gold Project in British Columbia on November 5. The Bralorne Project — a historic high-grade underground gold operation in BC's Bridge River gold camp — is Talisker's flagship asset, and the PEA marks a key development milestone as the company moves toward potential financing discussions at current gold prices above $4,100 per ounce.

headline: HONEY BADGER SILVER CONFIRMS 500ppm GERMANIUM AT NANISIVIK — Silver-Pyrite Zone and Critical Mineral Potential Established in Nunavut
source_name: Honey Badger Silver / Junior Mining Network
snippet: Honey Badger Silver (TSXV: TUF) confirmed silver-bearing massive pyrite mineralization at the Nanisivik Mine on Baffin Island, Nunavut, with field assays returning values exceeding 500 parts per million germanium — a critical mineral under Chinese export controls. The company has nine drill rigs active on a planned 90,000-metre program targeting both silver resources and the previously unassessed germanium potential within the former zinc-lead-silver mine's pyrite zones.

headline: GORDON MINING COMPLETES TUNGSTEN TAIL ACQUISITION — Rare Industrial Metal Added in New Mexico; Partial Share Consideration
snippet: Gordon Mining completed its acquisition of TT Minerals LLC — which holds the Tungsten Tail Project in Sierra County, New Mexico — on November 2, under an agreement dated October 19, 2026, with partial consideration paid in common shares. The deal adds exposure to tungsten, a critical industrial metal used in hard alloys, cutting tools, and defence applications, to Gordon Mining's portfolio.

headline: MERZ: EUROPE MUST BUILD CRITICAL MINERAL STOCKPILES — German Chancellor Warns of Supply Vulnerabilities as China REE Pause Nears Expiry
snippet: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called on Europe to build strategic stockpiles of critical raw materials to reduce exposure to supply disruptions, according to a Reuters report cited by Mining.com. The statement comes as China's expanded rare earth export control pause expires November 10 and continues a pattern of Western policy responses to supply chain vulnerabilities highlighted by Beijing's restrictions on dysprosium, terbium, and other heavy rare earth elements.
